newsitem.title: CHINA: China shuts 60,000 polluting enterprises in 1996.
newsitem.headline: China shuts 60,000 polluting enterprises in 1996.

text.p: China shut down 60,000 heavily polluting enterprises in 1996 in a mass campaign to curb damage to the environment, the Xinhua news agency quoted a senior Chinese official as saying.

The closures were "unprecedented whether in developing countries or developed ones", the official agency quoted Xie Zhenhua, director of the National Environmental Protection Agency (NEPA) as saying in a report late on Wednesday.
"As a developing country, China attaches great importance to the integration of the environment and economic development," Xie told a U.N. meeting on the environment in Kenya.
The closure of the 60,000 polluting plants showed China's determination to achieve sustainable development, Xie said.
Last September, Chinese officials announced they would spend up to 320 billion yuan ($38.6 billion) over the next five years to curb pollution and limit damage to the environment.
State media has said most of the plants targeted in a nationwide crackdown on major polluters have been producers of paper, fertilisers, electroplates or sulphur products.
Rivers and lakes across China are lined with tens of thousands of factories, many of which are small and inefficient and have little or no waste water treatment facilities.
Some of the world's highest levels of air pollution have been recorded by Chinese cities and acid rain is common.
